verdict.rationale: Homebrew installs each package version once into its own keg in a global Cellar and symlinks it into the prefix, so a shared single on-disk copy is used across projects (Brewfiles declare dependencies but draw from the same global install). Nothing shows the store is content-addressable (hash-keyed or deduplicated by content). missing for 10: evidence of content-addressable storage, documented cross-project deduplication semantics, independent or hands-on corroboration of disk savings.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a shared content-addressable store so the same dependency version is stored once on disk across all projects

citations.quote: It installs each package into its own keg inside the Cellar, then symlinks its files into the prefix
